fit: olive oil vehicle in a spirulina motor experiment
assessment: Lesioned rats received vehicle or spirulina in oral olive oil. Rotarod retention was measured for different active treatment groups. The lesion comparator used oil and the report does not establish its grade or assess clinical posture.

fit: olive oil vehicle in a transgenic A53T motor experiment
assessment: Four-week T-006 treatment improved time on the rotarod compared with vehicle in transgenic mice. The experiment assigns T-006 in oil versus oil and does not assess clinical postural instability.

fit: shared olive oil vehicle in a 6-OHDA mouse motor experiment
assessment: Methods and Figure 5 give rotarod retention and induced rotations. Olive oil was present in both the lesion comparison and the T-006 arm. Oil grade and a clinical Parkinson posture measure are absent.

fit: olive oil vehicle in a 6-OHDA rat experiment
assessment: The motor experiment randomized lesioned rats to T-006 in olive oil or vehicle. The separate mouse experiment used other comparisons. Neither isolates the requested culinary exposure or measures clinical postural instability.

fit: sage tea mouth rinse with sparse oral pain reporting
assessment: The randomized advanced-cancer trial recorded baseline mouth and swallowing pain. The authors omitted both items from their comparisons because few participants reported them. Sage rinse results for dry mouth give no pain effect.

fit: combined standardized ginger and ginkgo extract in rat maze
assessment: The combined preparation increased open-arm behavior at a lower dose and decreased approach at a higher dose. The 1 mg/kg finding was inconclusive. The effect of freshly grated ginger alone and clinical anxiety were not assessed.

fit: ginger and ginkgo extract ratios in rat maze
assessment: The 2.5:1 mixture at 1 mg/kg increased open-arm behavior. Other ratios gave no detected effect. This experiment does not isolate ginger and differs from the earlier experiment at the same total dose.
